newsitem.title: INDIA: STERLITE INDIAN PLANT DECISION AFTER STUDY - GOVT.
newsitem.headline: STERLITE INDIAN PLANT DECISION AFTER STUDY - GOVT.

text.p: The Tamil Nadu state government said on Friday it would decide on the reopening of Sterlite Industries (India) Ltd's copper smelter only after detailed examination of a suspected gas leak.
"We haven't got a report as to where the gas emanated from," M. Karunanidhi, chief minister of the state, told reporters in the southern town of Tiruchirapalli.
"We will take a decision only after a detailed report from the committee comes. We will not be hasty in reopening the factory."
Hemant Jalan, chief executive officer of Sterlite's smelter in the Tamil Nadu port town of Tuticorin, told Reuters the company expected a "quick and fair decision" from the state government.
"Our pollution control measures are open for scrutiny at any time. Our only aim now is to get back on stream, which itself would take almost a week, and wipe out our backlog and losses," Jalan said.
Sterlite operates India's only private-sector smelter, with an annual capacity of 100,000 tonnes. The smelter began operations in December 1996.
Last month, Sterlite was asked to close down its operations after suspected gas emissions in which more than 100 workers in a nearby factory were reportedly hospitalised.
The company strongly denies the charge.
Company officials have said that the closure was costing the company 25 million rupees ($700,280) every day.
The state government set up an expert committee to examine the emissions. The experts from Annamalai University are scheduled to meet with state authorities on Saturday.

Local newspapers reported on Thursday that blood samples collected from the affected victims did not reveal any toxic substances, particularly sulphur dioxide, the gas that was suspected to have leaked from Sterlite's plant. ($1 = 35.7 rupees)
